p.src: Now Niu Wenzhong, seeing that Gaizhou was lost, had no choice but to flee the city. Escorted by Yu Yulin, Guo Xin, Sheng Ben, and Sang Ying, he ran straight into Li Kui and Lu Zhishen, who were leading infantry to block his path. Li Kui shouted, “By Vanguard Song’s command, I’ve been waiting a long time for you defeated scoundrels!” He charged, swinging his twin axes; as his hands rose and the blades fell, Guo Xin and Sang Ying were promptly cut down. Niu Wenzhong was terrified out of his wits and, before he could react, Lu Zhishen struck him with his monk’s staff, smashing helmet and head together and knocking him from his horse. More than two hundred men were slaughtered to the last; only Yu Yulin and Sheng Ben managed to break desperately through at an angle and escape. Lu Zhishen said, “Let those two blockheads go! Let them carry back the news.” They then cut off the three heads, seized the saddled horses, helmets, and armor, and went straight into the city to present their spoils.

p.src: Meanwhile, Song Jiang’s main army entered Gaizhou. He immediately issued orders that the fires be extinguished first and that no harm be done to the inhabitants. All the commanders came forward to report their achievements. Vanguard Song ordered the soldiers to display the severed heads as a warning at the city gates, and at daybreak he posted proclamations to reassure the people. He brought the entire army into Gaizhou to encamp and rewarded the officers and men. In the register of merit, the achievements of Shi Xiu, Shi Qian, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao were specially recorded. At the same time, a memorial was written and submitted to the imperial court. Having taken Gaizhou, they sent all the wealth, silks, gold, and treasure from the government storehouses under escort to the capital, and wrote a dispatch reporting the matter to Grand Commandant Su. The twelfth month was now drawing to a close. While Song Jiang attended to military affairs, three or four days passed unnoticed, until word suddenly came that Zhang Qing had recovered and had arrived with An Daoquan to present himself for duty. Song Jiang said delightedly, “Excellent. Tomorrow is New Year’s Day in the fifth year of Xuanhe, and now we can all be together.”

p.src: At dawn the next day, all the commanders donned court robes and official headgear. Song Jiang led his brothers in facing the imperial palace from afar and offering New Year’s homage. After completing the rite of five bows and three prostrations, they removed their official robes and headgear and each put on a red brocade battle robe. The ninety-two chieftains, together with the newly surrendered commander Geng Gong, assembled in perfect order to offer festive greetings and pay their respects to Song Jiang. Vanguard Song laid out a magnificent feast to celebrate the occasion and bestow rewards. The brothers took turns raising cups to Song Jiang and wishing him long life. After several rounds of wine, Song Jiang said to the commanders, “Through the strength of all my brothers, three cities have been restored to the realm. And now, on New Year’s Day, we are gathered together in happiness—truly a rare blessing. My only regret is that Gongsun Sheng, Huyan Zhuo, Guan Sheng, the eight naval commanders including Li Jun, Chai Jin and Li Ying who are guarding Lingchuan, and Shi Jin and Mu Hong who are guarding Gaoping—these fifteen brothers are not here before me. It saddens me deeply.” He immediately summoned officers from the army and assigned them more than two hundred men for transport duty, rewarding each group separately. That very day he had them carry sheep and wine by different routes to Weizhou, Lingchuan, and Gaoping, to deliver them to the commanders guarding those cities and report the victory. Before he had finished giving his instructions, it was suddenly reported that the commanders guarding the three cities had sent men to offer New Year’s greetings. All of them, obeying the vanguard’s command and burdened with military duties, were unable to come in person to pay homage. Song Jiang was overjoyed and said, “To receive this news is just like seeing them face-to-face.” He rewarded the messengers, then drank heartily with his brothers until all were thoroughly drunk.

p.src: Tumbling like willow catkins, flake upon flake like goose down. In the air, flocks of white egrets fly; over the river, pale gulls wheel and tumble. Drifting into courtyards, they turn and twirl, shaped by the wind; Gleaming upon spears and halberds, they sparkle more brightly in the sunlight. A thousand mountains are built of jade, enough to leave the woodcutter bewildered and unable to find his trail; Ten thousand homes are clad in silver, inspiring many a recluse to fashion splendid verses. Indeed, all say an abundant year is good—but what manner of blessing is its auspicious snow? At the frontier many bear halberds; auspicious snow is welcome, but not too much.

p.src: At this point Xiao Rang, the “Earthly Literary Star,” said to the assembled chieftains, “Snowflakes have several names according to their form: a single flake is called a bee; two are goose down; three are a cluster of three; four are a gathering of four; five are called plum blossoms; and six are called six-petaled flowers. Snow is formed by the congealing of the yin breath, and therefore has six petals, corresponding to the yin number. After the Start of Spring, the flakes are all mixed plum-blossom forms, and there are no more six-petaled ones. Although today is already the Start of Spring, we are still at the meeting of winter and spring, so the flakes have either five or six petals.” Hearing this explanation, Yue He went beneath the eaves and caught the falling flakes on the sleeve of his black robe. When he examined them, the snowflakes truly had six petals; one petal had not yet entirely vanished and still retained sharp angles, while some flakes already had only five. Yue He cried out repeatedly, “It’s true! It’s true!” Everyone crowded around to look, but a blast of warm breath from Li Kui’s nose struck the snowflakes and melted them away. Everyone burst out laughing. The commotion startled Vanguard Song, who came out and asked, “What are you brothers laughing at?” They replied, “We were looking at the snowflakes, but the ‘Black Whirlwind’ melted them with the breath from his nose.” Song Jiang laughed too and said, “I have already ordered wine to be prepared in the Yichun Garden. Let us all go enjoy the snow together.”

p.src: To the east of the prefectural offices stood a garden called Yichun Garden. Within it was the Rain-Fragrance Pavilion, before which grew several junipers, cypresses, pines, and plum trees. That evening the chieftains talked and laughed boisterously in the Rain-Fragrance Pavilion, passing cups and tally sticks back and forth. Before they knew it, dusk had fallen and the lamps and candles were lit. When Song Jiang was merry with wine, the casual talk turned to the hardships he had suffered in former days and how greatly he had depended upon his brothers. “I was merely a petty clerk in Yuncheng who committed a grave crime. Again and again, amid a thousand spears and ten thousand blades, in straits where death seemed certain and life barely possible, you brothers risked your own lives to rescue me. When Brother Dai Zong and I were being escorted to the execution ground at Jiangzhou, there was not the slightest doubt that we were doomed. Yet today I have become a servant of the realm and am able to exert myself in its cause. Looking back upon those former days, it all seems truly like a dream!” As Song Jiang reached this point, tears began to stream down his face. Dai Zong, Hua Rong, and the other brothers who had shared those perils also shed tears when they heard these words.

p.src: By then, Li Kui had drunk several cups too many. As the wine took hold, he talked with the others, but his eyelids gradually drooped; resting his face upon both arms, he fell asleep. Suddenly a thought crossed his mind: “The snow outside still hasn’t stopped.” Though the thought was only in his mind and his body had not moved at all, he seemed already to have walked out of the pavilion. Looking outside, he found it strange: “Why, there’s no snow. I’ve only been sitting in there all this time! Let me go over that way and take a stroll.” He left Yichun Garden and was soon outside the prefectural city, when he suddenly remembered: “Oh no! I forgot my battle-axes!” But when he felt at his waist, there they were, tucked into his belt. He blundered onward without regard for north or south, and after traveling he knew not how far, saw a lofty mountain ahead. Before long he reached the foot of the mountain. A man emerged from a hollow, wearing a folded-corner cap and a pale-yellow Daoist robe. Coming forward, he smiled and said, “If you wish to take a stroll, General, go around this mountain; you will find something there to delight you.” Li Kui asked, “Brother, what is this mountain called?” The scholar replied, “This mountain is called Heavenly Pool Ridge. When you return from your excursion, General, meet me here again.” Li Kui followed his directions and went around the mountain, whereupon he suddenly saw a manor beside the road. Hearing a tremendous uproar within, Li Kui burst inside. A dozen or more men, all armed with cudgels and weapons, were smashing tables and benches and breaking the household furnishings to pieces. One burly fellow among them cursed, “You old ox, hurry up and hand your daughter over to be my wife, and that will be the end of it. But utter half a word of refusal, and every one of you will die!” Entering from outside and hearing this, Li Kui’s heart blazed like fire and smoke seemed to pour from his mouth. He roared, “You damned rogues! How dare you try to seize another man’s daughter?” The men shouted back, “We want his daughter. What damned business is it of yours?” Li Kui flew into a rage, drew his battle-axes, and hacked at them. Strangely enough, they could not withstand even a single blow: with one stroke he felled two or three of them. The rest tried to flee, but Li Kui overtook them and, with six or seven blows in quick succession, sent them tumbling in every direction until corpses covered the ground. Only one escaped, running away outside. Li Kui rushed farther inside and found a pair of doors tightly shut. He kicked them open and saw within a white-haired old man and an old woman, both weeping. Seeing Li Kui burst in, they cried, “Disaster! They’ve broken in!” Li Kui shouted, “I am one who intervenes when he sees injustice. I have killed all those damned rogues out front. Come and see for yourself.” The old man tremblingly followed him out and looked, but then seized Li Kui and said, “Though you have rid us of those villains, you will still embroil me in a lawsuit with the authorities.” Li Kui laughed. “You old man, you clearly don’t know your Black Grandfather. I am Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind of Liangshan Marsh. At present I am serving with my elder brother Song Gongming under imperial command in the campaign against Tian Hu. They are drinking in the city now, but I grew restless and came out for a stroll. Never mind those few damned rogues—even if I killed several thousand, what damned law could touch me?” Only then did the old man wipe away his tears and say, “If that is so, all is well! Please come inside and sit down, General.” Li Kui went inside, where a table had already been laid with wine and food. The old man helped Li Kui into the seat of honor, filled a bowl to the brim with wine, and offered it in both hands, saying, “You saved my daughter, General. Please drain this cup.” Li Kui took it and drank, and the old man urged another bowl upon him. After he had drunk four or five bowls in succession, the old woman who had been weeping earlier appeared, leading a young woman forward. Together they folded their hands and bowed in greeting.

p.src: The old woman said, “You serve under Vanguard Song, General, and are such a remarkable hero. If you do not disdain her ugliness, we would gladly give our daughter to you as your wife.” At these words Li Kui sprang to his feet. “You filthy, crooked old wretch! Do you think I killed those damned scoundrels just now because I coveted your daughter? Shut your damned mouth at once, and stop farting such nonsense!” With a single kick he overturned the table and ran out the door. Just then, a powerfully built man appeared from the other side, brandishing a long-handled saber. Striding rapidly after him, the man roared, “You black rogue there, stop! Why did you kill all those brothers of mine just now? We wanted that family’s daughter. What business was it of yours?” Leveling his long-handled saber, he charged straight at Li Kui. Li Kui flew into a rage, swung his axes to meet him, and fought the man for more than twenty bouts. Unable to prevail, the man knocked aside the battle-axes, dragged his long-handled saber behind him, and fled as swiftly as if flying. Li Kui pursued him closely. After passing through a wood, he suddenly saw a great many palace halls. The man raced to the front of a hall, cast away his long-handled saber, and vanished among the crowd. Then a voice from the hall cried, “Li Kui, show no insolence! Have him come forward for an imperial audience.” Li Kui suddenly realized, “This is the Hall of Civil Virtue. I came here with Brother Song for an imperial audience the other day. This is where the Emperor resides.” Again a voice from the hall commanded, “Li Kui, prostrate yourself at once!” Li Kui concealed his battle-axes and went forward to look. Far off, he saw the Emperor seated in the hall, with many officials arrayed before it. Li Kui solemnly bowed three times toward the throne, then thought, “Oh no! I’m one bow short!” The Son of Heaven asked, “Why did you kill so many people just now?” Kneeling, Li Kui replied, “Those scoundrels tried to seize another man’s daughter by force. Your servant was overcome with anger and killed them.” The Son of Heaven said, “Li Kui intervened upon seeing injustice and destroyed a band of villains. His righteousness and courage are commendable. I pardon you of all guilt and appoint you General of the Palace Guard.” Li Kui rejoiced inwardly. “So the Emperor is truly this wise and discerning!” He knocked his head upon the floor more than ten times in succession, then rose and stood below the hall.

p.src: Before long, Cai Jing, Tong Guan, Yang Jian, and Gao Qiu appeared. All four knelt and prostrated themselves, memorializing: “Song Jiang now commands the troops sent against Tian Hu, yet he tarries and will not advance, spending every day drinking. We humbly beg Your Majesty to punish him.” When Li Kui heard this, the nameless fire of rage in him flared three thousand fathoms high. Unable to contain himself, he rushed forward with both axes and, with one stroke apiece, hewed off their heads, shouting: “Your Majesty, do not listen to what those traitorous ministers say! My brother Song has already taken three cities in succession. His army is now encamped at Gaizhou and is about to march. How dare they deceive you so?” When the civil and military officials saw that four great ministers had been killed, they all moved to seize Li Kui. Brandishing his two axes, Li Kui cried: “Anyone who dares seize me will end up like those four!” At that, no one dared lay a hand on him. Li Kui laughed loudly: “What satisfaction! What satisfaction! Those four traitorous ministers have finally met their end today. I shall go and tell brother Song.” He strode out of the palace. Suddenly another mountain appeared before him. Looking at it, he saw that it was the very place where he had just met the scholar. The scholar was still standing before the slope. He came forward to meet him and said with a smile: “Did the general enjoy his excursion?” Li Kui replied: “You should know, elder brother, that I have just killed four traitorous ministers.” The scholar smiled. “So that was it! I originally dwelt between the Fen and Qin rivers and only happened to wander here recently. Knowing that you and your companions cherish loyalty and righteousness, I have something important to tell you. Commander Song is now campaigning against Tian Hu. I have a ten-character maxim by which Tian Hu may be captured. You must remember it firmly and convey it to Commander Song.” Then he recited to Li Kui: “To destroy Tian Hu’s clan, one must join with Qiong, the arrowhead.” He repeated it five or six times in succession. Finding the scholar’s words reasonable, Li Kui followed him and rehearsed the ten characters aloud. The scholar then pointed into the woods and said: “Over there, an old woman is sitting among the trees.” But when Li Kui turned to look, the scholar had already vanished. Li Kui said: “How quickly he has gone! I shall go into the woods and see who is there.” He rushed into the woods, and there indeed sat an old woman. When Li Kui drew near and looked, he saw that it was none other than Iron Ox’s own mother, sitting blankly upon a green stone with her eyes closed. Li Kui ran forward and embraced her. “Mother! Where have you been suffering all this time? Iron Ox thought a tiger had eaten you, yet here you are today!” His mother said: “My son, I was never eaten by a tiger.” Weeping, Li Kui said: “Iron Ox has now accepted the imperial amnesty and truly become an officer. Brother Song’s great army is now stationed in the northern city. Iron Ox will carry Mother there on his back.” As they were speaking, a tremendous crash suddenly sounded. A striped great tiger leapt from the woods, roared, lashed its tail, and sprang straight at them. Startled, Li Kui raised his broad axes and hacked at the tiger. He struck with such force that both axes cleaved empty air; pitching forward, he fell across the wine table in the Rain-Fragrance Pavilion of Yichun Garden.

u.src: Before long, Cai Jing, Tong Guan, Yang Jian, and Gao Qiu appeared. All four knelt and prostrated themselves, memorializing: “Song Jiang now commands the troops sent against Tian Hu, yet he tarries and will not advance, spending every day drinking. We humbly beg Your Majesty to punish him.”

When Li Kui heard this, the nameless fire of rage in him flared three thousand fathoms high. Unable to contain himself, he rushed forward with both axes and, with one stroke apiece, hewed off their heads, shouting: “Your Majesty, do not listen to what those traitorous ministers say!
My brother Song has already taken three cities in succession. His army is now encamped at Gaizhou and is about to march. How dare they deceive you so?”
When the civil and military officials saw that four great ministers had been killed, they all moved to seize Li Kui.
Brandishing his two axes, Li Kui cried: “Anyone who dares seize me will end up like those four!”
At that, no one dared lay a hand on him.
Li Kui laughed loudly: “What satisfaction!
What satisfaction!
Those four traitorous ministers have finally met their end today. I shall go and tell brother Song.”
He strode out of the palace.
Suddenly another mountain appeared before him. Looking at it, he saw that it was the very place where he had just met the scholar.
The scholar was still standing before the slope. He came forward to meet him and said with a smile: “Did the general enjoy his excursion?”
Li Kui replied: “You should know, elder brother, that I have just killed four traitorous ministers.”
The scholar smiled. “So that was it!

I originally dwelt between the Fen and Qin rivers and only happened to wander here recently. Knowing that you and your companions cherish loyalty and righteousness, I have something important to tell you.
Commander Song is now campaigning against Tian Hu. I have a ten-character maxim by which Tian Hu may be captured.
You must remember it firmly and convey it to Commander Song.”
Then he recited to Li Kui: “To destroy Tian Hu’s clan, one must join with Qiong, the arrowhead.”
He repeated it five or six times in succession.
Finding the scholar’s words reasonable, Li Kui followed him and rehearsed the ten characters aloud.
The scholar then pointed into the woods and said: “Over there, an old woman is sitting among the trees.”
But when Li Kui turned to look, the scholar had already vanished.
Li Kui said: “How quickly he has gone!
I shall go into the woods and see who is there.”
He rushed into the woods, and there indeed sat an old woman.
When Li Kui drew near and looked, he saw that it was none other than Iron Ox’s own mother, sitting blankly upon a green stone with her eyes closed.
Li Kui ran forward and embraced her. “Mother!
Where have you been suffering all this time?
Iron Ox thought a tiger had eaten you, yet here you are today!”
His mother said: “My son, I was never eaten by a tiger.”
Weeping, Li Kui said: “Iron Ox has now accepted the imperial amnesty and truly become an officer.
Brother Song’s great army is now stationed in the northern city. Iron Ox will carry Mother there on his back.”
As they were speaking, a tremendous crash suddenly sounded. A striped great tiger leapt from the woods, roared, lashed its tail, and sprang straight at them.

Startled, Li Kui raised his broad axes and hacked at the tiger. He struck with such force that both axes cleaved empty air; pitching forward, he fell across the wine table in the Rain-Fragrance Pavilion of Yichun Garden.

p.src: Song Jiang and his brothers were recalling events of former days and had reached the most engrossing part of their conversation. At first they had noticed Li Kui dozing with his head upon the table but paid him no heed. Suddenly there came a crash: still asleep, Li Kui had slapped the table with both hands, overturning the bowls and dishes and splashing broth over both sleeves, while he continued to shout: “Mother, the tiger has fled!” Opening his eyes, he saw the lamps and candles blazing brightly and all his brothers seated around him, still drinking there. Li Kui said: “Bah! So it was only a dream—yet a most satisfying one!” Everyone laughed. “What sort of dream was it? Why has it pleased you so?” Li Kui first told them that he had dreamed of his mother, who had never died after all, and that just as they were happily speaking, a tiger had interrupted them. Everyone sighed. Li Kui then told how he had killed the villains and kicked over the tables. Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, and Shi Xiu, seated on the other side, clapped their hands and cried: “Splendid!” Li Kui laughed. “There is better still!” He went on to tell how he had killed the four traitorous ministers Cai Jing, Tong Guan, Yang Jian, and Gao Qiu. Everyone clapped and shouted with one voice: “Splendid! Splendid! A dream like that was well worth dreaming!” Song Jiang said: “Brothers, quiet yourselves. Those were merely words spoken in a dream; what importance can they have?” Li Kui, now at the most exciting part of his tale, rolled up his sleeves and clenched his fists. “Why the devil must we be quiet? Never in my life have I done anything so exhilarating. And there was another strange thing: I dreamed that a scholar told me something like, ‘To destroy Tian Hu’s clan, one must join with Qiong, the arrowhead.’ He said those ten characters were the essential secret for defeating Tian Hu and told me to remember them well and pass them on to Commander Song.” Neither Song Jiang nor Wu Yong could unravel their meaning. An Daoquan, who was present, heard the three characters “Qiong, the arrowhead” and was just about to speak when Zhang Qing caught his eye. An Daoquan smiled faintly and said nothing. Wu Yong said: “This is a most extraordinary dream. As soon as the snow clears, we may advance.” The drinking party then broke up, and all retired to rest. Nothing further happened that night.

p.src: The next day the snow cleared. Song Jiang took his seat in the command tent and conferred with Lu Junyi and Strategist Wu. They resolved to divide the army into two columns and advance east and west. The eastern column would cross Huguan and take Zhaode, proceed by way of Lucheng and Yushe straight to the rear of the rebels’ stronghold, then pass through Dagu to Linxian, where both armies would unite for the final assault. The western column would take Jinning, emerge from Mount Huo, capture Fenyang, and proceed through Fenxiu, Pingyao, and Qixian directly to the northwest of Weisheng. The two armies would join at Linxian, take Weisheng, and capture Tian Hu. The officers were then assigned to the two columns as follows:

p.src: Once Song Jiang had completed his assignments, he conferred again with Lu Junyi, saying, “Now that we are to divide our forces here and campaign east and west, which front would you like to take, worthy brother?” Lu Junyi replied, “The command of troops and dispatch of generals rest with you, elder brother. I shall obey your strict orders—how would I dare choose for myself?” Song Jiang said, “Even so, let us put it to the will of Heaven. After fixing the number of men in each force, we shall write the two destinations on lots and each draw one.” Pei Xuan thereupon prepared two lots, one marked east and the other west. Song Jiang and Lu Junyi burned incense and prayed, and Song Jiang drew one of them. Because Song Jiang drew that particular lot, several more heroic and valiant commanders were destined to join the ranks of the three armies; and before Five Dragons Mountain, a wondrous tale of extraordinary arts was to unfold. But which destination did Vanguard Song draw? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
